metadata.title: Robinhood CEO Responds to AMC Tokenization Criticism

content.text:
Last Updated:
11 hours ago
Robinhood CEO Responds to AMC Tokenization Criticism
Robinhood Chief Executive Vlad Tenev defended the company's push into tokenized stocks in a CNBC interview Wednesday. Tenev's remarks come on the heels of fiery criticism from AMC Chief Executive Adam Aron, whose company's shares are among those being tokenized.
Tenev said companies can't control the financial products created around their shares once public. “Issuers should have control and do have control over the rights and obligations of the stock that they issue, but that doesn’t mean they control everything about it,” he said. “In particular, they don’t control other companies issuing their own securities that reference those shares.”
Stock tokens represent publicly traded shares on a blockchain network. Holders however don't receive a direct stake in a company and the associated protections guaranteed to equity investors. And in Robinhood's case, stock tokens are structured as debt securities.
